correctness.rationale: Function-field irreducibility follows from the valuation −1 of R(t) at t=0. Complete Jacobian algebra determines the r torus singular points with no coordinate-boundary exceptions. For p|m, the separable r-Kummer normalization after purely inseparable Frobenius untwisting and tame Riemann–Hurwitz give genus (r−1)/2. Branch uniqueness, nonzero second derivative in characteristic p≠2, transitive μ_r symmetry and the genus–delta formula force every formal germ U²−V^q. The all-n derivation is independent of the 150 finite prime-field spot checks.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2001 same-family paper expressly excludes these primes; the 2015 Klein-curve automorphism work treats nonsingular curves; the detailed 1998 Klein quartic treatment focuses on a special case and alternative stable models. published-finding corpus and literature searches by equation, determinant exponent, cusps, Kummer normalization and characteristic seven did not identify an implication covering the full bad-characteristic theorem. This is best-knowledge rather than independently certified originality.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently worded trinomial Kummer-curve theorem could already contain the general result.
The n=3,p=7 case is classical adjacent material; originality attaches to uniform all-n all-bad-primes cusp and genus classification, not that special example.
The 2018 later work and broader curve literature were reviewed in relevant portions, not proved exhaustively noncovering.

value.rationale: It fills a structurally motivated characteristic boundary of a standard family: previously smooth plane models become exactly r unibranch wild cusps; local delta and complete normalization genus collapse are determined for every exponent n and exceptional prime, including extreme rational and elliptic degenerations. The exact Kummer-cover normalization also supports arithmetic and degeneration analysis. The result is materially more informative than detecting a bad discriminant or one isolated example.
